meta.label: Everyday clothing
meta.attribution: Curated from public sustainability reports, certifications (Fair Trade, GOTS, B Corp), supply-chain transparency indices, and labor-rights coverage - not audited data. Brands change; the cheapest, lowest-impact garment is usually the one you already own. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare everyday clothing by labor practices, environmental impact, disclosure, and durability.

axes.label: Labor practices
axes.question: Do stronger labor practices matter more?

axes.label: Environmental impact
axes.question: Does lower environmental impact matter more?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Patagonia
products.description: A premium outdoor and basics brand with strong repair, reuse, Fair Trade and environmental disclosure programs.

environment.note: Patagonia reports broad use of recycled/organic inputs and strong environmental initiatives, but it still sells new technical apparel at global scale.

labor.note: Patagonia says more than 90% of its line is made in Fair Trade Certified factories, benefiting 85,000+ workers.

transparency.note: Its footprint pages disclose factory, material and program information at a level uncommon in mainstream apparel.

durability.note: Worn Wear supports trade-in, resale and repair, explicitly aiming to keep gear in use longer.

accessibility.note: Premium outdoor pricing keeps it less accessible than mainstream basics, even with used Worn Wear options.

products.name: People Tree
products.description: A fair-trade fashion pioneer centered on organic cotton, artisan partners and transparent production.

environment.note: People Tree describes GOTS-certified organic cotton and environmentally friendly production as central to the brand.

labor.note: People Tree is listed by WFTO as a mission-driven fair trade business working with artisans and farmers.

transparency.note: The brand says its pieces are traceable in a transparent supply chain and names its fair-trade positioning plainly.

durability.note: Natural-fiber, artisan-made garments suggest better longevity than trend-led fast fashion, though no universal repair guarantee is offered.

accessibility.note: Mid-to-high ethical-fashion pricing and UK/EU availability make it less accessible than global fast fashion.

products.name: Armedangels
products.description: A European basics brand with a detailed impact report, Fair Wear performance and certified preferred-material programs.

environment.note: Armedangels' 2025 impact report details preferred materials and circularity work, with gaps still acknowledged.

labor.note: The 2025 impact report reports Fair Wear Foundation Leader status and living-wage pilot work.

transparency.note: The brand publishes a dedicated 2025 impact report with supplier, material and worker-rights metrics.

durability.note: Its impact reporting includes circular systems and repair activity, but repair is not as central as Nudie or Patagonia.

accessibility.note: Mid-price European basics are more accessible than premium ethical labels but less accessible than mass retailers.

products.name: Kotn
products.description: A B Corp basics brand built around direct Egyptian cotton sourcing and community investment in cotton-growing regions.

environment.note: Kotn describes direct cotton sourcing from family-run farms in Egypt and lower-impact material choices.

labor.note: B Lab lists Kotn as a certified B Corp with a 102.6 overall impact score.

transparency.note: Kotn publishes materials and sourcing pages; B Corp certification adds third-party accountability but not full farm-to-factory public data.

durability.note: The brand sells staple cotton basics rather than micro-trend pieces, but does not offer a Patagonia-style repair system.

accessibility.note: Mid-price basics are more reachable than many ethical labels, but still above fast-fashion pricing.

products.name: Nudie Jeans
products.description: A denim brand with annual sustainability reports, a production guide, organic cotton focus and free repair program.

environment.note: Nudie Jeans publishes annual sustainability reports covering materials, production and product impacts.

labor.note: Its reports and policies cover supplier conditions and social compliance, though denim supply chains remain complex.

transparency.note: Nudie publishes reports and policies, including sustainability reporting and production information.

durability.note: The brand offers free repairs for Nudie jeans through repair shops and repair kits.

accessibility.note: Premium denim pricing and repair-shop geography limit accessibility despite strong repair value.

products.name: Outerknown
products.description: A US apparel brand using preferred fibers and Fair Labor Association accreditation, with premium positioning.

environment.note: Outerknown's current sustainability page commits to regenerative or recycled materials and circular products under its 2030 roadmap.

labor.note: Fair Labor Association lists Outerknown as a participating company that became Fair Labor Accredited in 2017.

transparency.note: Outerknown publishes a 2030 roadmap and goals for supplier transparency, fair compensation and circularity, but says its first progress report is still forthcoming.

durability.note: Outerknown operates US-only Outerworn resale and a SEA JEANS warranty, currently two years for post-February 2026 purchases rather than a broad repair program.

accessibility.note: Premium US positioning limits accessibility even where the brand is available online.

products.name: Pact
products.description: An organic-cotton basics brand using Fair Trade USA and GOTS claims at a more accessible ethical-fashion price point.

environment.note: Pact centers its product line on GOTS-certified organic cotton and lower-impact basics.

labor.note: Pact says products are made in Fair Trade Certified factories and partners with Fair Trade USA.

transparency.note: Pact discloses certifications and sustainability partners, but less factory-level detail than transparency leaders.

durability.note: Soft organic basics are useful staples, but the brand does not offer a major repair or take-back durability program.

accessibility.note: Pact is cheaper than most ethical labels while still above the lowest fast-fashion price floor.

products.name: Reformation
products.description: A trend-led womenswear brand with unusually detailed impact reporting, lower-impact fiber work and some repair/resale infrastructure.

environment.note: Reformation's sustainability report and Commons profile describe preferred-fiber work, climate accounting, circularity pilots and remaining impact from fashion-cycle volume.

labor.note: The brand reports supplier standards and responsible-sourcing work, but public evidence is stronger on materials and climate than on living-wage outcomes across the chain.

transparency.note: Reformation publishes detailed annual impact reporting and product sustainability claims, with more disclosure than many fashion peers.

durability.note: Resale and repair channels support longer use, while trend-led collections keep durability evidence mixed.

accessibility.note: Premium pricing and a womenswear focus limit affordability, though online distribution is broad.

products.name: Girlfriend Collective
products.description: A recycled-material activewear brand known for inclusive sizing, take-back/resale programs and comparatively strong labor signals.

environment.note: Brand and third-party profiles emphasize recycled polyester, nylon and cotton plus take-back and resale, while noting incomplete emissions-target evidence.

labor.note: Eco-Stylist cites SA8000-certified manufacturing and living-wage indicators, stronger than many athleisure peers.

transparency.note: The brand provides material and factory claims, though third-party profiles note gaps in full target and impact disclosure.

durability.note: Performance basics, resale and recycling programs support longer use, though synthetic activewear still carries wear and microfiber concerns.

accessibility.note: Mid-priced direct-to-consumer activewear with broad size range and global shipping, but still above budget apparel prices.

products.name: Tentree
products.description: A B Corp casualwear brand built around tree planting, preferred materials and public sustainability reporting.

environment.note: Tentree's B Corp profile centers the brand on planting trees per purchase and an earth-first apparel mission.

labor.note: B Lab lists Tentree as a certified B Corp; labor-specific public detail is weaker than its climate/tree story.

transparency.note: Tentree's current Impact Report page frames disclosure across Transparency, Climate, Product, Nature and People.

durability.note: Tentree's Circularity program accepts used Tentree and non-Tentree items for recycling or reuse and supports peer-to-peer resale, but not a full repair service.

accessibility.note: Tentree's resale shop offers verified pre-loved pieces at reduced prices, making the brand more accessible than premium-only ethical apparel.

products.name: Eileen Fisher
products.description: A premium womenswear brand known for circular design, B Corp certification and a long-running Renew take-back program.

environment.note: B Lab describes Eileen Fisher's responsible lifecycle model, including eco-preferred materials and Renew take-back.

labor.note: B Lab lists Eileen Fisher as a certified B Corp, reflecting third-party review of social and environmental practices.

transparency.note: B Corp certification and sustainability communications provide useful accountability, though not every supplier detail is public.

durability.note: B Lab notes Eileen Fisher takes clothes back through Renew for resale, remaking or recycling, a strong circularity signal.

accessibility.note: Premium womenswear pricing makes it less accessible despite resale and Renew options.

products.name: Organic Basics
products.description: A Copenhagen-designed basics brand with B Corp certification and public impact reports on materials and factories.

environment.note: Good On You credits Organic Basics for a high proportion of lower-impact materials including organic cotton, while still rating it only moderate overall.

labor.note: Good On You notes certified final production and audits, but no evidence that Organic Basics ensures living wages across its supply chain.

transparency.note: B Lab lists DG Organic Basics as a certified B Corp, but public factory-level detail remains thinner than top transparency leaders.

durability.note: Basics and lower-impact materials suggest solid everyday durability, but no major repair/resale loop is central.

accessibility.note: Good On You lists Organic Basics as a premium-price brand shipping worldwide, so access is broad but cost remains limiting.

products.name: ThredUp
products.description: A large US online secondhand platform that makes resale easier at scale, while still depending on the quality and labor history of garments already made.

environment.note: ThredUp's impact materials frame resale as extending garment life and avoiding some new production; its 2026 report says secondhand is growing faster than apparel retail overall.

labor.note: Resale avoids some new manufacturing demand, but ThredUp does not verify the original labor conditions of every garment it resells.

transparency.note: ThredUp publishes resale and impact reports, including ESG strategy updates, but resale-impact claims still depend on displacement assumptions.

durability.note: The platform recirculates used garments and reports how items are listed, reused or recycled; actual durability varies by brand and condition.

accessibility.note: Online resale offers broad price ranges and many brands, but availability depends on size, condition, search friction and US-centric logistics.

products.name: Vinted
products.description: A peer-to-peer secondhand marketplace that makes used clothing cheap and mainstream, with strong circular potential but limited control over original garment production.

environment.note: Vinted's sustainability page says 76% of orders avoided the purchase of a new item and reports 1,607 ktCO2e avoided in 2025.

labor.note: Vinted can reduce demand for new garments, but peer-to-peer resale does not verify or remediate the labor conditions behind the original item.

transparency.note: Vinted publishes impact reporting and climate methodology, but its marketplace still relies on user behavior and self-reported replacement effects.

durability.note: Secondhand resale extends the usable life of garments, but condition and longevity depend on the item, seller accuracy and buyer care.

accessibility.note: Vinted's peer-to-peer model is built around low-cost secondhand access and operates across multiple European and UK markets.

products.name: Wear what you already own longer
products.description: The highest-leverage clothing choice when the garment already works: delay replacement, repeat outfits, and treat new buying as optional.

environment.note: EEA's current textiles topic page says circular design can reduce textile impacts by retaining value, extending lifecycles and increasing recycled materials.

labor.note: Keeping an existing garment avoids commissioning new production; it does not remediate the original garment's labor conditions.

transparency.note: EEA frames longer use, reuse and repair as circular strategies, while the original garment's supply chain may still remain unknown.

durability.note: EEA says durable, high-quality and circular textiles are needed as fast fashion and low collection rates hinder reuse and recycling.

accessibility.note: No-new-purchase reuse requires no new transaction when the garment still fits the need; EEA's textile work prioritizes longer active use over more throughput.

products.name: Repair, hem, or alter existing clothes
products.description: Mending, tailoring, zipper replacement, hemming, and visible repair can turn a neglected garment back into a useful one.

environment.note: EEA says circular textile strategies need longer lifecycles, reuse and repair to reduce production and waste pressure.

labor.note: Repair shifts some value to local or specialist repair work instead of new cut-and-sew production, though access and wages vary.

transparency.note: iFixit publishes step-by-step apparel repair guides, making the work itself more inspectable than most new-garment supply chains.

durability.note: Common repairs such as fixing holes, buttons, and zippers can restore usability rather than sending wearable clothing to waste.

accessibility.note: iFixit maintains free clothing and apparel repair guides, but skill, tools, time, and access to tailoring still make repair less universal than wearing as-is.

products.name: Clothing swaps / Buy Nothing groups
products.description: A free or near-free reuse route for everyday clothing, best when it replaces a new purchase rather than adds more browsing.

environment.note: Clothing swaps and gifting keep items in active use; EEA's current textile work names longer use and reuse as core circular strategies.

labor.note: Community reuse reduces demand for new garments but does not verify the labor conditions of the original item.

transparency.note: Buy Nothing is a local gift-economy model, so transparency is interpersonal and item-by-item rather than brand-audited.

durability.note: Fashion Revolution swap and mending events explicitly combine clothes swaps with repair and upcycling.

accessibility.note: Buy Nothing groups are free and local, but inventory, sizing, moderation, and geography vary a lot.

products.name: eBay pre-owned clothing
products.description: A huge mainstream resale route for used clothing, especially useful when you search for durable brands and avoid new-with-tags overconsumption.

environment.note: eBay's current sustainable-commerce reporting says 2025 recommerce activity avoided emissions, diverted waste and created positive economic impact.

labor.note: Resale can displace some new production, but marketplace purchases do not verify or improve the original garment's labor conditions.

transparency.note: eBay reports recommerce impacts and methodology at platform level, but individual clothing condition and provenance still depend on seller listings.

durability.note: eBay reports recommerce remains central to its sustainable-commerce impact; the durability benefit depends on keeping pre-owned items in active use.

accessibility.note: eBay is a global marketplace with broad price ranges, search tools, and a large used-apparel supply.

products.name: Poshmark
products.description: A large resale marketplace for everyday and branded clothing, strongest when used for actual secondhand replacement rather than extra impulse buying.

environment.note: Poshmark frames resale as extending the life of clothing and making fashion more circular.

labor.note: Peer resale reduces some demand for new production but does not audit or remediate original garment labor conditions.

transparency.note: Posh Protect covers not-as-described, damaged, missing, or inauthentic items, but condition and material transparency still depend on seller listings.

durability.note: The circular value depends on keeping wearable items in use and avoiding resale-as-overconsumption.

accessibility.note: Poshmark's app-based marketplace makes secondhand branded clothing easy to search and buy in its served markets.

products.name: Depop
products.description: A youth-oriented resale marketplace that can make secondhand feel desirable, with better impact methodology than many resale peers.

environment.note: Depop says secondhand buying reduces waste and cuts greenhouse-gas emissions associated with new production.

labor.note: Depop reduces some demand for new fashion but cannot verify the labor conditions behind the original items being resold.

transparency.note: Depop's impact hub links its environmental-impact methodology and progress updates, making its resale-impact claims more inspectable than many peers.

durability.note: Depop's stated mission is to keep existing fashion in use longer, though item quality depends on sellers and original brands.

accessibility.note: Depop is app-based and accessible for many younger shoppers, but availability and price vary by region and seller behavior.

products.name: Rent the Runway
products.description: A rental route for special-occasion and rotating wardrobes; useful when it displaces new purchases, weaker if it increases shipping-heavy consumption.

environment.note: Rent the Runway says its model enables customers to buy less and wear more, but rental impact depends on displacement, logistics, and cleaning.

labor.note: Rental can reduce new production demand, but it does not directly verify labor conditions for the original garments.

transparency.note: RTR keeps a public impact page with its displacement and waste-diversion goals, though rental benefits still depend on actual avoided purchases.

durability.note: Rental works best with garments durable enough for repeated wear and maintenance across many customers.

accessibility.note: Rental can be expensive and occasion-driven, so it is less accessible than resale or wearing what you own.

products.name: Nuuly
products.description: A mainstream US clothing-rental subscription from URBN, useful for temporary wardrobes or occasions when it genuinely replaces buying new.

environment.note: Nuuly says rental extends clothing life through rewearing, repair and end-of-life upcycling, but rental benefits depend on avoided purchases, cleaning and shipping.

labor.note: Rental can reduce demand for newly made garments, but Nuuly does not verify labor conditions for each original garment in the shared closet.

transparency.note: Nuuly publishes a sustainability page and rental FAQs, though it gives less supply-chain detail than leading apparel transparency programs.

durability.note: Nuuly describes professional stain treatment, mending and inspection before garments return to the shared closet.

accessibility.note: Nuuly rents six items per month for a fixed monthly price, making it approachable for frequent renters but expensive compared with using or buying secondhand.

products.name: Armoire
products.description: A US clothing-rental membership aimed at workwear and everyday variety, strongest when it substitutes for trend-driven new purchases.

environment.note: Armoire frames rental as a way to displace new garment creation, but circular benefits still depend on displacement, logistics and garment care.

labor.note: The rental model may lower new-production demand, but it does not itself disclose labor conditions for the original garments.

transparency.note: Armoire has a public sustainability note and FAQs, but limited brand-by-brand material or supplier disclosure.

durability.note: Rental memberships depend on garments surviving repeated cleaning, shipping and wear across many users.

accessibility.note: Armoire's current FAQ lists capsule memberships from $89-$129 per month and an unlimited plan at a higher monthly price.

products.name: By Rotation
products.description: A peer-to-peer fashion rental and resale app that lets people lend existing wardrobes rather than rely on platform-owned inventory.

environment.note: Ellen MacArthur Foundation profiles By Rotation as a peer-to-peer rental model that keeps existing clothing in use.

labor.note: Peer-to-peer rental can reduce new-production demand, but it does not verify labor conditions behind the original garments.

transparency.note: By Rotation has published an impact-scale explainer and is externally profiled as a circular-fashion case study.

durability.note: The model rewards high-quality garments that can be lent repeatedly, while fit, damage and cleaning remain user-managed risks.

accessibility.note: The app supports renting, lending and pre-loved sales, with access dependent on local inventory and peer participation.

products.name: HURR
products.description: A UK fashion-rental and resale marketplace with B Corp certification and a stronger circular-fashion disclosure trail than many rental peers.

environment.note: HURR's mission is to extend clothing lifespans through renting, monthly refreshes and pre-owned purchasing.

labor.note: B Corp certification evaluates worker, community, governance and environmental practices, though it does not audit every original garment supply chain.

transparency.note: HURR reports B Corp status and frames its rental/resale model publicly through sustainability and terms pages.

durability.note: HURR's rental and resale model depends on garments that can be lent, returned and resold rather than worn once.

accessibility.note: The core rental offer is UK-oriented and occasion-led, so access is narrower than resale marketplaces or local reuse.

products.name: Mercari pre-owned clothing
products.description: A broad secondhand marketplace where clothing is one category among many; useful for affordable reuse when shoppers buy intentionally.

environment.note: Mercari positions resale and reuse as its core sustainability lever for circulating goods rather than discarding them.

labor.note: Secondhand buying can reduce new-production demand, but it does not verify the labor conditions behind the original clothing.

transparency.note: Mercari publishes sustainability and impact-reporting pages, but item-level clothing claims depend on individual sellers.

durability.note: Reuse value depends on listing quality and garment condition, with no single durability standard across the marketplace.

accessibility.note: Mercari lists thousands of new and used items, including clothing, with marketplace pricing often below retail.

products.name: Grailed
products.description: A resale marketplace strongest for menswear, streetwear, vintage and designer pieces, where buying used can replace new high-impact fashion purchases.

environment.note: Grailed frames peer-to-peer resale as a way to find new homes for unwanted or pre-worn garments instead of buying new.

labor.note: Resale can reduce demand for new fashion, but it does not verify labor conditions behind the original garments being resold.

transparency.note: Grailed publishes trust, safety and purchase-protection information, but seller listing detail varies.

durability.note: Its focus on designer, vintage and archival pieces often favors garments with resale value, though quality still varies by seller.

accessibility.note: Grailed offers millions of listings from thousands of designers, but prices skew higher for collectible and hype-driven goods.

products.name: Etsy vintage clothing
products.description: A broad route for vintage and handmade clothing, strongest when shoppers use it for durable secondhand pieces rather than mass-produced novelty items.

environment.note: Vintage clothing keeps existing garments in use, and Etsy separately publishes a climate-impact plan for marketplace emissions.

labor.note: Vintage resale can reduce new-production demand and support small sellers, but it does not verify labor behind original garments.

transparency.note: Etsy's vintage policy requires vintage items to be at least 20 years old and says Etsy may ask sellers for supporting information.

durability.note: The vintage category rewards garments that have already survived years of use, but condition and authenticity vary by seller.

accessibility.note: Etsy's marketplace offers many vintage-clothing shops and filters, but pricing, sizing and return policies vary widely.

products.name: Thrift+
products.description: A UK online secondhand-fashion service that handles resale logistics and can direct proceeds to the seller, credit, or charity.

environment.note: Thrift+ says its mission is to make shopping and reselling pre-loved clothes easier and end fashion waste.

labor.note: Secondhand resale can reduce new-production demand, but it does not verify labor conditions behind the original garments.

transparency.note: Thrift+ explains its resale process and terms, including how proceeds are split among the seller, Thrift+ and suggested charity.

durability.note: The service quality-checks items and recirculates accepted clothing, though durability depends on the original garment.

accessibility.note: Thrift+ makes clearing out and shopping secondhand easier in the UK, but its service region is narrower than global resale marketplaces.

products.name: SOJO repair
products.description: A UK repair and alterations platform for brands and customers, strongest as infrastructure that makes repair feel normal and convenient.

environment.note: SOJO's stated work is to extend clothing life through repair and alterations, a circular route WRAP identifies as a key textiles model.

labor.note: SOJO is a B Corp certified repair service, supporting repair labor while not auditing the original garment supply chain.

transparency.note: SOJO publicly describes its B Corp status, repair technology and brand-service model.

durability.note: Repair directly extends the usable life of garments and WRAP identifies repair as a circular business model for keeping textiles in use.

accessibility.note: SOJO is most visible as a UK repair infrastructure and brand partner, so access depends on geography and participating brands.

products.name: The Seam
products.description: A UK care-and-repair service that connects clothing, footwear and bag repairs to local makers or postal repair routes.

environment.note: The Seam's service is organized around repairing items and returning them ready to wear again.

labor.note: The Seam connects customers with local Makers, supporting skilled repair work rather than only new-garment production.

transparency.note: The Seam lays out a clear quote, delivery and repair process, though maker-level labor detail is limited.

durability.note: Repair and alteration services directly address fit, wear and damage so existing garments can stay in use longer.

accessibility.note: The service offers photo-based quotes and local or postal options, but availability and price are UK-centered.

products.name: Clothes Doctor
products.description: A clothing-care and repair-education route focused on washing less aggressively, refreshing, protecting fibers and making garments last longer.

environment.note: Clothes Doctor positions its care products around washing less, refreshing between wears and keeping clothes longer.

labor.note: Care and repair can reduce new-purchase pressure, but it does not verify labor conditions behind the original garments.

transparency.note: Clothes Doctor publishes product and care guidance, but it is a care brand rather than a full apparel supply-chain disclosure route.

durability.note: Its care system is explicitly aimed at reducing overwashing and protecting garments so wardrobes last longer.

accessibility.note: At-home care products and practical repair advice are easier to use repeatedly than specialist alteration services, though they still require effort.

products.name: Fixing Fashion
products.description: A free open repair-learning project for caring, fixing and upgrading clothes, useful when the best purchase is no purchase.

environment.note: Fixing Fashion teaches people to care, fix and repair clothes to address waste connected with fashion.

labor.note: DIY repair avoids some new-production demand and builds local repair skill, while not claiming to solve original supply-chain labor harms.

transparency.note: One Army describes Fixing Fashion as a public project sharing knowledge and techniques for care, repair and upgrading clothing.

durability.note: The project is explicitly built around extending garment life through repair and upgrade skills.

accessibility.note: The tutorials are free online resources, making the route more accessible than paid repair services if a person has time and basic tools.

products.name: Arc'teryx / ReBIRD
products.description: Premium technical clothing with unusually strong durability, repair, and resale infrastructure, but high prices and outdoor-performance materials.

environment.note: Arc'teryx ReBIRD resale takes back and refurbishes unused gear to extend active life; the brand points to its 2025 climate report for current disclosures.

labor.note: Arc'teryx reports sustainability and responsible-manufacturing work, but premium technical supply chains still carry materials and supplier risk.

transparency.note: Arc'teryx points users to current sustainability disclosures including its 2025 climate report.

durability.note: ReBIRD resale items are authenticated, repaired, refreshed, and covered for practical product lifespan.

accessibility.note: Arc'teryx is expensive and performance-oriented, so access is much narrower than mainstream basics despite resale channels.

products.name: The North Face / Renewed
products.description: A mainstream outdoor brand with a growing renewed/resale route, useful for durable outerwear but still part of VF's large apparel footprint.

environment.note: The North Face says Renewed is a refurbished and upcycled product platform for buying used and trading in unwanted gear.

labor.note: Parent company VF publishes responsibility reporting and factory lists, but brand-specific living-wage evidence remains limited.

transparency.note: VF publishes reporting and factory-list materials, giving some group-level visibility into The North Face supply chain.

durability.note: The Renewed store sells used jackets, outerwear, and apparel restored to like-new condition.

accessibility.note: The North Face is widely available, but Renewed inventory and sizes vary and prices are above many everyday basics.

products.name: Cotopaxi
products.description: A mission-led outdoor brand with B Corp status, impact reporting, preferred-material goals, and repair work, though still a premium new-product seller.

environment.note: Cotopaxi's 2025 impact report, published in 2026, reports material sourcing, deadstock use, PFAS elimination, climate work and circularity limits.

labor.note: Cotopaxi is a certified B Corp and public benefit corporation, with B Lab scoring covering workers and governance.

transparency.note: Cotopaxi's 2025 impact report cites GRI alignment, materiality work, public compliance documents and verification methods for several data areas.

durability.note: Cotopaxi's 2025 report discusses product circularity, repair, resale and design-for-serviceability while naming practical tradeoffs.

accessibility.note: Cotopaxi is globally visible online but priced as premium outdoor/lifestyle gear, limiting budget accessibility.

products.name: prAna
products.description: A better-than-mainstream active/outdoor clothing brand with Fair Trade history, preferred materials, and packaging work.

environment.note: prAna reports organic, recycled, responsible-down, cellulosic-fiber, and plastic-free packaging milestones across its sustainability timeline.

labor.note: prAna says it launched Fair Trade Certified apparel early and is a Fair Labor Association member.

transparency.note: prAna says it published a supply-chain list and participates in Canopy and responsible-packaging initiatives.

durability.note: prAna has piloted repair and resale and sells active/outdoor apparel where longer wear is part of the value proposition.

accessibility.note: prAna is easier to find than small ethical labels but remains mid-to-premium priced compared with mass basics.

products.name: L.L.Bean
products.description: A durable mainstream option for practical outdoor and casual basics, with preferred-material progress but less radical transparency than values-led brands.

environment.note: L.L.Bean reports preferred-material use in outerwear and activewear, including recycled polyester and organic cotton.

labor.note: L.L.Bean publishes supplier and forced-labor policy information, but disclosure is still compliance-led rather than living-wage proof.

transparency.note: L.L.Bean publishes product sustainability and supplier-policy pages, though not the full depth of leading transparency brands.

durability.note: L.L.Bean explicitly designs products to be durable rather than disposable, arguing longer-lasting products reduce waste.

accessibility.note: L.L.Bean is broadly available in the US online and through stores, with prices below many premium technical brands but above fast fashion.

products.name: Decathlon
products.description: A high-accessibility global sports retailer with useful repair and eco-design programs, but huge production scale and ongoing supply-chain risks.

environment.note: Decathlon reports net-zero-by-2050 commitments, eco-design work and a push toward second-life, rental and repair, while acknowledging major value-chain impacts.

labor.note: Decathlon publishes forced-labor and ethical-recruitment policies, but disclosure is not the same as evidence of living wages across the supply chain.

transparency.note: Decathlon publishes annual ESG and sustainable-development reports, making it more inspectable than many budget retailers.

durability.note: Decathlon's circularity work includes repair, second-life products and product recyclability, which supports longer use for some categories.

accessibility.note: Decathlon's value proposition is broad, affordable sports access through its own retail and online channels.

products.name: Levi's
products.description: A mainstream denim brand with stronger durability and reporting than many apparel peers, but still a large global producer.

environment.note: Levi Strauss publishes sustainability goals and metrics on water, climate, materials and circularity, but denim remains resource-intensive.

labor.note: Its 2024 goals report says 66% of key Tier 1 suppliers had well-established worker-management committees.

transparency.note: Levi Strauss publishes sustainability reports, CDP responses, SASB tables and goal progress updates.

durability.note: Denim and repairable basics give Levi's a durability advantage over trend-led fast fashion, though no universal free repair loop is central.

accessibility.note: Levi's is widely available through stores, wholesale and resale, but pricing sits above the cheapest fast-fashion floor.

products.name: Nike
products.description: A dominant global sportswear brand with extensive sustainability disclosure and supplier programs, but massive scale and complex labor exposure.

environment.note: Nike reports work on carbon, circularity, waste and water, but the brand's global scale keeps absolute impact high.

labor.note: Nike says 75% of strategic supplier facilities measured and improved worker engagement and 87% had safe, healthy workplaces in FY24.

transparency.note: Nike publishes sustainability data and responsible-supply-chain metrics, but not enough to make every factory-level outcome visible.

durability.note: Nike shoes and technical gear can last well, but the brand is not primarily built around repair, resale or buy-less durability.

accessibility.note: Nike's global retail footprint and wide price ladder make it accessible, although many products are premium-priced.

products.name: adidas
products.description: A major sportswear brand with mature reporting, supplier programs and some preferred-material progress, but still a high-volume global apparel business.

environment.note: adidas publishes annual sustainability reporting and environmental progress, but high-volume footwear and apparel still carry material supply-chain impact.

labor.note: adidas says it works with suppliers worldwide on fair labor, safe working conditions and environmental responsibility.

transparency.note: The 2025 annual report discloses sourcing concentration, including 92% of volume produced in Asia.

durability.note: Sportswear and footwear can be durable, but adidas is not primarily repair-led and still sells trend and performance cycles.

accessibility.note: adidas is globally available through stores, online and wholesale, with outlet and sale channels improving access.

products.name: lululemon
products.description: A global athletic-apparel brand with durable technical products, public impact reporting and circularity pilots, but high synthetic-material exposure.

environment.note: FY24 impact reporting and the 2030 agenda include preferred materials, supplier renewable-energy targets and circularity goals, but the assortment remains synthetic-heavy.

labor.note: lululemon reports responsible supply-chain programs and supplier engagement, but public evidence is not as strong as dedicated fair-trade or living-wage leaders.

transparency.note: The company publishes annual impact reporting, goals and progress updates, giving shoppers more visibility than many mainstream apparel brands.

durability.note: Core value is durable technical activewear, and the impact agenda includes repair and resale expansion targets.

accessibility.note: The brand is widely available globally, but premium prices make it less accessible than mass-market athletic apparel.

products.name: Gap / Old Navy
products.description: A mainstream basics and family-clothing group with improving disclosure and materials targets, but still conventional high-volume retail.

environment.note: Gap Inc.'s 2025 report highlights 100% more-sustainable cotton and 65% recycled polyester, but the model remains high-volume apparel retail.

labor.note: Gap says 100% of strategic Tier 1 facilities invest in RISE, reaching nearly 113,000 workers in 2025.

transparency.note: Gap publishes impact reports, a factory list, code-of-vendor-conduct assessment findings and CDP disclosures.

durability.note: Gap and Old Navy basics are useful staples, but the group is not repair-led and includes trend-led low-cost lines.

accessibility.note: Old Navy and Gap are broadly available and frequently discounted, making this one of the more accessible mainstream options.

products.name: Target apparel
products.description: Accessible U.S. mass-market clothing through Target owned and national brands, with supplier-transparency work but limited durability leadership.

environment.note: Target reports sustainability governance, supply-chain programs and material initiatives, but mass retail assortment and volume keep environmental performance modest.

labor.note: Target maintains responsible supply-chain standards and factory programs, though public evidence does not establish living-wage leadership for apparel workers.

transparency.note: Target publishes supplier and traceability information, including supply-chain transparency pages and sustainability reporting.

durability.note: The assortment includes useful basics, but low-cost fashion and private-label turnover are not durability-centered.

accessibility.note: Target has very high U.S. accessibility through stores, online ordering and low- to mid-priced apparel.

products.name: Walmart apparel
products.description: Lowest-price mass-market apparel with unmatched U.S. access, broad ESG programs and weak durability and overconsumption signals.

environment.note: Walmart's ESG reporting covers climate, sourcing and waste work, but low-price high-volume apparel remains structurally impact-intensive.

labor.note: Supplier policies and responsible-sourcing programs exist, but public evidence does not demonstrate strong living-wage outcomes for apparel supply chains.

transparency.note: Walmart publishes ESG reporting and corporate policies, but apparel-specific product-level transparency is limited compared with leaders.

durability.note: Low prices maximize access but often signal shorter-lived basics rather than repairable or longevity-focused apparel.

accessibility.note: Walmart is one of the most accessible apparel sources in the U.S. through stores, online ordering and very low entry prices.

products.name: ASOS
products.description: A major online fashion retailer with public Fashion with Integrity targets, but still a high-volume trend-led model.

environment.note: ASOS has Scope 3 reduction and materials commitments, but its own strategy acknowledges almost all emissions come from Scope 3 supply-chain activity.

labor.note: ASOS's 2025 modern-slavery statement says forced labour is a strategic pillar of its Human Rights strategy and describes 2024-2025 actions with IndustriALL, ITF and brand-partner due-diligence work.

transparency.note: ASOS's 2025 statement says it sourced from 21 countries, 441 active Tier 1 and 2 factories and 164 suppliers, with supply-chain visibility published through Open Supply Hub and a downloadable factory list.

durability.note: Commons rates ASOS insufficient, citing overproduction, fossil-fuel synthetics and no strategic repair/resale program to keep garments out of landfill.

accessibility.note: ASOS is easy to use globally online and covers a wide price/style range, making access high despite sustainability tradeoffs.

products.name: Mango
products.description: A global high-street fashion brand with sustainability planning and traceability work, but still tied to trend volume.

environment.note: Mango publishes climate and decarbonisation commitments, while acknowledging the need to transform its whole value chain and product design.

labor.note: Mango's sustainability materials discuss responsible supply-chain management, but public evidence does not establish living-wage leadership.

transparency.note: Mango says its sustainability plan includes work toward full traceability, including raw-material-level traceability.

durability.note: Mango offers better-made basics than ultra-fast fashion, but no large repair or resale system anchors durability.

accessibility.note: Mango is widely available online and through international stores at mid/high-street pricing.

products.name: American Eagle / Aerie
products.description: A familiar US mall brand with some cotton, viscose and climate progress, but still a large trend-and-promo apparel retailer.

environment.note: Stand.earth says AEO has strong foundations for supply-chain decarbonization but still needs near-term renewable-energy targets and saw Scope 3 growth.

labor.note: AEO publishes responsible-sourcing goals and supplier expectations, but this does not demonstrate living-wage outcomes across the apparel supply chain.

transparency.note: AEO publishes ESG goals and progress, including cotton, viscose, polyester and nylon sourcing progress.

durability.note: Denim and basics can last longer than microtrend pieces, but AEO is not a repair-centered brand.

accessibility.note: AEO and Aerie are highly accessible in the US through malls, online sales and frequent promotions.

products.name: Abercrombie & Fitch / Hollister
products.description: A revived mall-fashion group with public supplier and environmental programs, but moderate transparency and high-volume retail tradeoffs.

environment.note: A&F says Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers complete Higg FEM annually and publishes climate, energy, chemical and supply-chain programs.

labor.note: A&F publishes vendor codes, policies and supply-chain materials, but public evidence does not establish living-wage leadership.

transparency.note: A&F's sustainability hub links active factory listings, reports, policies, vendor code and supply-chain act disclosures.

durability.note: Core denim and basics can be durable, but the group does not center repair, resale or long-life guarantees.

accessibility.note: Broad online and mall availability plus recurring promotions make the brand accessible for many US shoppers.

products.name: Marks & Spencer clothing
products.description: A UK mainstream retailer with stronger quality, Plan A reporting and repair/reuse signals than many high-street peers.

environment.note: M&S Plan A includes SBTi-validated targets across Scope 1, 2 and Scope 3 categories and commitments on materials and waste.

labor.note: The 2025 ESG report covers responsible sourcing and overseas sourcing standards, though living-wage proof remains limited.

transparency.note: M&S publishes ESG reporting and Plan A commitments, making its clothing strategy more legible than many mass retailers.

durability.note: M&S Restored by SOJO offers door-to-door repair and restoration so customers can wear M&S clothing for longer.

accessibility.note: M&S is a highly accessible UK clothing source with broad store/online reach and mid-market pricing.

products.name: Amazon Essentials apparel
products.description: A cheap and extremely accessible private-label basics line inside Amazon's broader marketplace system.

environment.note: Amazon publishes supply-chain and sustainability programs, but private-label apparel remains a high-volume low-price marketplace model.

labor.note: Amazon says it seeks safe and fair supply chains, but public Amazon Essentials-specific wage and factory outcome evidence is limited.

transparency.note: Amazon has corporate supply-chain disclosure, but Amazon Essentials product-level supply-chain transparency is weak compared with apparel leaders.

durability.note: Low-cost basics can be useful, but the brand has no major repair, resale or longevity system.

accessibility.note: Amazon Essentials is extremely easy to buy online, with low prices and broad size/category coverage.

products.name: Fashion Nova
products.description: A social-media-native fast-fashion brand with very low prices and very weak public accountability signals.

environment.note: Fashion Nova's current about page emphasizes more than 1,000 new arrivals weekly and speed-led trend turnover, with no comparable environmental disclosure.

labor.note: Fashion Nova's supply-chain disclosure relies on vendor agreements and a reserved right to audit, with no living-wage or supplier-list evidence.

transparency.note: FTC's 2025 refund notice says Fashion Nova was barred from suppressing customer reviews after allegations it hid reviews under four stars.

durability.note: Fashion Nova describes itself around speed, trends and disruption, not repair, resale or long-life garment systems.

accessibility.note: The brand is highly accessible online and built around very low prices, discounts and influencer-driven demand.

products.name: Temu apparel marketplace
products.description: An ultra-cheap marketplace apparel option with severe forced-labor compliance and accountability concerns.

environment.note: Good On You rates TEMU's planet performance very poor, citing its ultra-fast-fashion model, few lower-impact materials and no supply-chain emissions action evidence.

labor.note: Anti-Slavery International's 2026 forced-labour import-ban overview names cotton and textiles among UFLPA-affected sectors, keeping weak-traceability apparel a high-risk floor.

transparency.note: Anti-Slavery International's 2026 overview says UFLPA places proof burdens on importers and shows why ultra-cheap direct-to-consumer apparel remains hard to verify.

durability.note: Ultra-low marketplace prices and trend-driven listings give little evidence of durable garment design or repair/reuse systems.

accessibility.note: Temu's appeal is extreme price accessibility and global app/web reach, which is exactly why the accountability risks matter.

products.name: Primark
products.description: A very low-price high-street retailer with some traceability and materials progress, but still tied to fast-fashion volume and low prices.

environment.note: Primark reports 74% of clothing units contained recycled or more sustainably sourced materials in 2024/25, but only about 5% were circular by design.

labor.note: Primark's own report emphasizes traceability and supplier programs, but the low-price high-volume model keeps labor-risk concerns material.

transparency.note: Primark reports 100% of clothing, textile and footwear suppliers onboarded to its traceability programme up to Autumn/Winter 2025.

durability.note: Only 5% of clothing unit sales were circular by design in the 2024/25 report, so durability remains weak despite progress.

accessibility.note: Primark's core proposition is extremely low prices in physical stores, making it highly accessible where stores exist.

products.name: Boohoo / Debenhams Group
products.description: An online fast-fashion group with a public factory list and modern-slavery policies, but very weak climate, labor and circularity signals.

environment.note: Stand.earth gives Boohoo an F overall, citing no net-zero transition plan, no supply-chain renewable electricity target and no thermal-energy transition evidence.

labor.note: Debenhams Group's current policy hub lists its 2025 Modern Slavery Statement plus child-labour, fair-wages, modern-slavery, responsible-purchasing and subcontracting policies; low score remains because past Leicester abuses and fast-fashion purchasing pressure still shape the risk context.

transparency.note: Stand.earth says Boohoo shares a supplier list but does not make tiers clear and has not yet fully mapped its supply chain.

durability.note: Stand.earth gives Boohoo an F on low-carbon and longer-lasting materials, with no clear repair/resale scale or production-reduction link.

accessibility.note: The group is built around low-price online access across brands including boohoo, boohooMAN and PrettyLittleThing.

products.name: Goodwill thrift stores
products.description: A high-access secondhand default: strongest when it replaces new buying, with local quality and pricing varying by store.

environment.note: Goodwill frames responsible reuse as a way to prevent products from going to waste while funding its training and employment mission.

labor.note: Goodwill's annual report documents its employment, training and community mission, though local member organizations vary.

transparency.note: Goodwill Industries International publishes annual impact, 990 and audited financial statement materials, but store-level operations differ by member organization.

durability.note: Buying secondhand extends garment life; Goodwill describes usable donated items being resold through stores, outlets and online channels.

accessibility.note: Goodwill's thrift-store model is broadly accessible in the US, including lower-cost stores and outlet formats, though inventory is inconsistent.

products.name: Savers / Value Village thrift stores
products.description: A mainstream thrift option with real reuse value and nonprofit-partner funding, but a for-profit model rather than a charity store.

environment.note: Savers Value Village says its model reduces waste by promoting reuse of textiles and household goods and recycling excess materials.

labor.note: The company reports generating revenue for nonprofit partners, but it remains a for-profit thrift chain rather than a worker-rights or living-wage clothing brand.

transparency.note: Savers publishes ESG and impact reporting for its reuse model and nonprofit-partner revenue, giving shoppers more visibility than many thrift chains.

durability.note: Secondhand shopping extends the useful life of existing garments, but item quality depends on donated inventory.

accessibility.note: Savers and Value Village operate as large thrift retailers with accessible store formats where present, though coverage is less universal than online marketplaces.

products.name: Universal Standard
products.description: A size-accessibility leader worth including for fit equity, but with weak public sustainability and supply-chain disclosure.

environment.note: Universal Standard says it uses premium fabrics and sustainable options where possible, but Good On You rates it 'We Avoid' for insufficient public impact information.

labor.note: Good On You says the brand provides insufficient information about actions on people, planet and animals, so labor confidence remains limited.

transparency.note: Commons says Universal Standard has not published the amount of sustainability or production information expected for a brand its size.

durability.note: Universal Standard emphasizes engineered fit and garments that last through repeated wear and washing, but repair/resale systems are not central.

accessibility.note: Universal Standard's core accessibility strength is size range: it presents the brand as fashion from 00 to 40.

products.name: Lucy & Yak
products.description: A colorful UK slow-fashion option with impact reporting, Fair Wear membership and a resale/recycling route.

environment.note: Lucy & Yak publishes sustainability and impact reporting and says it works on carbon measurement, materials and keeping products in circulation.

labor.note: Fair Wear announced Lucy & Yak joined as a member in January 2026, bringing its code of labour practices into the brand's sourcing work.

transparency.note: Lucy & Yak's impact-reporting pages describe supplier partnerships, Sedex membership and carbon-footprint work, though disclosure is not as exhaustive as traceability-first brands.

durability.note: The Re:Yak PreLoved program lets UK customers return or recycle Yaks, supporting reuse and keeping garments in circulation.

accessibility.note: The brand offers casualwear with a strong body-inclusivity message, but it is less price-accessible than thrift or mass-market basics.

products.name: Finisterre
products.description: A repair-and-materials leader for outdoor clothing, strongest for buyers who need durable coastal/weather gear rather than general basics.

environment.note: Finisterre says 93% of its 2024 collection was made from organic, recycled or natural fibres, while acknowledging materials are its largest footprint lever.

labor.note: Finisterre's impact reporting covers factories and fair-working-condition work, but it is not primarily a living-wage proof brand.

transparency.note: Finisterre publishes impact reports, product-journey transparency work and B Corp certification information.

durability.note: Finisterre's Lived and Loved team repaired 2,095 items in 2024, including jackets, and expanded repair access.

accessibility.note: Finisterre sells premium outdoor clothing with repair support, but price and category focus make it less accessible than mainstream basics.

products.name: ASKET
products.description: A transparency-first slow-fashion basics brand: strong on origin and impact disclosure, weaker on price accessibility.

environment.note: ASKET publishes environmental impact data through its Impact Receipt, including CO2e, water, energy, packaging and shipping impacts.

labor.note: ASKET publishes supply-chain traceability and supplier detail, which improves accountability but is not the same as independent living-wage proof.

transparency.note: ASKET says it discloses supply-chain traceability, cost and environmental footprint information on every product page.

durability.note: ASKET's permanent-collection model and product refinement are designed around fewer, longer-use basics rather than seasonal churn.

accessibility.note: The model is premium and direct-to-consumer; price and limited retail presence make it less accessible than mass-market basics.

products.name: Quince
products.description: A useful skeptical benchmark: affordable and widely searched, but its ethical/sustainability claims have weak independent support.

environment.note: Quince says it values transparent materials and manufacturing, but Commons finds limited evidence for emissions measurement, reduction targets or verified offsets.

labor.note: Eco-Stylist says Quince fails basic ethical-fashion standards, including no concrete supplier disclosure or third-party labor certification evidence.

transparency.note: Commons says Quince does not publish supply-chain partners beyond general geography or share a public supplier code of conduct.

durability.note: Quince markets elevated staples, but independent reviews of its sustainability claims raise durability and accountability concerns, so durability stays only moderate.

accessibility.note: Quince's direct-to-consumer model emphasizes lower prices on cashmere, silk, linen and basics, making it accessible relative to many premium alternatives.

products.name: Madewell
products.description: A mainstream denim option with real resale and recycling programs, but not a slow-fashion or labor leader.

environment.note: Madewell's Do Well materials page points to sustainability reporting and denim recycling, but the brand remains a mainstream new-clothing retailer.

labor.note: Madewell has reported Fair Trade Certified denim goals, but public labor evidence is weaker than dedicated fair-trade apparel leaders.

transparency.note: Madewell publishes Do Well reporting and recycling pages, offering more public detail than opaque mall brands but less than traceability-first brands.

durability.note: Madewell Forever and Trade In Your Denim extend the life of Madewell and other denim through resale or recycling partners.

accessibility.note: Madewell is widely shoppable online and in US stores, with a lower price point than many slow-fashion denim brands.

products.name: Everlane
products.description: A once-independent transparency-focused basics brand whose 2026 sale to Shein materially weakens its values fit.

environment.note: Everlane remains a sustainability-oriented DTC brand, but the Shein acquisition adds major ownership and model concerns.

labor.note: The 2026 Shein acquisition materially weakens the labor-risk picture because Shein has a poor public labor record.

transparency.note: Everlane still publishes an impact report, but Shein ownership makes the 'radical transparency' claim harder to treat at face value.

durability.note: Everlane's quality claim survives in its brand positioning, but no major repair or resale system anchors the score.

accessibility.note: The acquisition is framed around global expansion and financial stability, but pricing is not ultra-fast-fashion cheap.

products.name: Uniqlo
products.description: A global mainstream basics retailer with better durability than many fast-fashion peers, but still a massive scale apparel business.

environment.note: Fast Retailing reports 2030 climate/material targets, but low-emission materials were still a minority of materials in fiscal 2025.

labor.note: Fast Retailing publishes human-rights commitments and monitoring, but its global supply chain still carries material labor-risk exposure.

transparency.note: Fast Retailing publishes a production-partner list to improve traceability.

durability.note: RE.UNIQLO Studio offers repair, remake, donation and recycling services in selected locations, supporting longer garment use.

accessibility.note: Uniqlo is globally available and affordable relative to ethical labels, with broad store and online reach.

products.name: H&M
products.description: A global fast-fashion giant with sector-leading climate disclosure for its peer group, but still built around high-volume low-cost apparel.

environment.note: Stand.earth gives H&M a B+ overall and says it has a 100% supply-chain renewable-electricity target, while flagging synthetics and shipping as gaps.

labor.note: H&M Group's 2025 modern-slavery statement covers FY2024-2025, publishes Tier 1 and 2 factory audit and grievance data, and says it came close to its no-recruitment-fee goal while acknowledging ongoing supply-chain risks.

transparency.note: Stand.earth gives H&M A+ for commitments and transparency and notes Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier lists plus detailed supply-chain energy data.

durability.note: Stand.earth gives H&M a C on low-carbon and longer-lasting materials, noting resale and rental pilots but no direct link to reducing production.

accessibility.note: Very broad global reach and low prices make H&M highly accessible.

products.name: Zara (Inditex)
products.description: Inditex's flagship fast-fashion brand: stronger climate and material work than the worst floors, but still tied to rapid trend production and uneven disclosure.

environment.note: Stand.earth gives Inditex a C overall, with strong targets and materials work but weak supplier decarbonization financing and rising shipping emissions.

labor.note: Clean Clothes Campaign says no fashion brand can say all its workers are paid a living wage, keeping labor risk material despite Inditex disclosures.

transparency.note: Stand.earth says Inditex has useful emissions disclosure but remains opaque on supplier lists and does not provide supply-chain energy data by tier.

durability.note: Stand.earth gives Inditex B+ on low-carbon and longer-lasting materials and notes Zara Pre-Owned in 17 markets, but no production-reduction link.

accessibility.note: Zara is globally available and relatively affordable, though not as cheap as ultra-fast-fashion floors.

products.name: Shein
products.description: The ultra-fast-fashion floor: very cheap and accessible, but with major labor, volume, waste and transparency concerns.

environment.note: Stand.earth gives Shein an F overall, citing 164% manufacturing-emissions growth, no supply-chain renewable target and heavy air-freight exposure.

labor.note: In a 2025 UK Parliament response, SHEIN described its audit and grading system and said two underage-labour cases found after October 2023 led to supplier termination; KnowTheChain still flags major forced-labour disclosure gaps.

transparency.note: SHEIN's 2025 Parliament response says SRS audit results are published in ESG reporting and gives audit-grade data, but scrutiny remains high because the company says it does not prohibit Chinese cotton where that use would not violate law.

durability.note: Stand.earth gives Shein D- on low-carbon and longer-lasting materials and says circularity efforts do not fundamentally address the business model.

accessibility.note: Shein's core appeal is extremely low prices, fast product turnover and global online access.

products.name: Patagonia Worn Wear
products.description: Patagonia's used-gear and repair route for buying secondhand Patagonia apparel, trading items in, and extending the life of existing clothing.

environment.note: Worn Wear is explicitly built around trade-in, used purchase and repair so Patagonia items stay in use longer.

labor.note: This route reduces demand for new production, but labor conditions still depend on Patagonia's underlying supply chain and the specific garment.

transparency.note: Patagonia publishes footprint and repair/trade-in information, and Worn Wear explains trade-in and used-product terms.

durability.note: The program is centered on repair, resale and keeping Patagonia gear in use rather than replacing it.

accessibility.note: Used Patagonia is usually cheaper than new, but the catalog is brand-limited and still outdoor-apparel focused.

products.name: REI Re/Supply
products.description: REI's member-focused used gear and apparel marketplace, useful for outdoor clothing when buying used is the main value choice.

environment.note: REI describes Re/Supply as a way for members to buy and trade in used gear and apparel, extending product life.

labor.note: Used resale lowers new-production demand, but it does not by itself verify the original labor conditions of each garment.

transparency.note: REI publishes Re/Supply eligibility and FAQ details, but item-level origin and repair history vary by product.

durability.note: The program is concentrated in outdoor gear and apparel designed for continued use, but condition varies by listing.

accessibility.note: Re/Supply makes used outdoor clothing available online and in store, but REI membership and inventory limits narrow access.

products.name: The RealReal
products.description: A large authenticated luxury-resale marketplace: better for keeping high-end clothing in circulation than for budget basics.

environment.note: The RealReal reports avoided water and greenhouse-gas impacts from keeping luxury items in circulation through resale.

labor.note: Resale reduces new luxury production demand, but the labor record depends on the original brand and The RealReal's own operations.

transparency.note: The company publishes sustainability and social-impact metrics, while individual garment supply-chain details remain brand-dependent.

durability.note: Luxury resale can favor longer-lived goods, but condition, repairability and material quality vary by listing.

accessibility.note: The marketplace is widely available online, but the luxury focus makes it less accessible than mainstream or thrift options.

products.name: Vestiaire Collective
products.description: A global fashion-resale marketplace with B Corp certification and published impact reporting, strongest for circular luxury rather than low-cost clothing.

environment.note: Vestiaire Collective publishes impact reporting around resale, circularity and avoided environmental impacts.

labor.note: B Corp certification covers broader governance and stakeholder practices, but original garment labor conditions vary by brand.

transparency.note: The company publishes impact reports and B Corp materials, giving more public method detail than many resale marketplaces.

durability.note: Luxury resale generally favors higher-value items worth recirculating, but condition and longevity still vary by listing.

accessibility.note: Vestiaire operates internationally online, but its luxury positioning limits low-price accessibility.

products.name: Carhartt Reworked
products.description: Carhartt's resale and trade-in path for durable workwear, useful when repair, longevity and lower waste matter more than fashion turnover.

environment.note: Carhartt says Reworked keeps gear on the job and reduces clothing waste, while its broader material footprint still has room to improve.

labor.note: Carhartt publishes corporate-responsibility policies and audit references, but independent ratings still leave labor-transparency gaps.

transparency.note: The Commons rates Carhartt Fair and flags limited supplier disclosure and incomplete emissions target evidence.

durability.note: Carhartt's Reworked program depends on durable garments retaining resale value after prior use.

accessibility.note: Carhartt workwear is widely available in the US, and Reworked can lower prices, but inventory varies.

products.name: MUD Jeans
products.description: A circular-denim specialist built around leasing, repair and recycling old jeans into new denim; high values fit, but more niche and premium.

environment.note: Circular-economy case studies describe MUD Jeans' model of recycling old jeans into new denim and reducing virgin-material demand.

labor.note: B Corp certification provides third-party evidence of broader stakeholder practices, including workers and governance.

transparency.note: MUD Jeans' circular model has multiple public case studies describing lease, return, repair and recycling mechanics.

durability.note: The lease and repair model includes free repair and take-back routes intended to extend garment use.

accessibility.note: MUD Jeans is a specialist denim brand with premium pricing and less mainstream availability than mass-market jeans.

products.name: GANNI
products.description: A recognizable fashion brand with B Corp certification and unusually explicit 'not sustainable' transparency, but still a premium new-clothing purchase.

environment.note: Good On You credits some lower-impact materials and climate commitments, while noting room for stronger tracking and impact reduction.

labor.note: B Corp certification gives third-party evidence across stakeholder categories, though it is not a garment-level labor audit.

transparency.note: GANNI's responsibility page explicitly says it does not identify as sustainable and frames the work as transparency and improvement.

durability.note: GANNI is a premium fashion brand rather than a repair-first or essentials-durability specialist, so longevity depends heavily on item choice.

accessibility.note: The brand is internationally available but premium-priced relative to mainstream apparel.

products.name: Lands' End
products.description: A mainstream family-basics option with durability and affordability strengths, but weaker public evidence on materials, emissions and supplier disclosure.

environment.note: The Commons rates Lands' End Low, citing high-impact materials and limited evidence of emissions-reduction targets despite some lower-impact material use.

labor.note: The Commons flags a lack of supplier disclosure and limited public labor evidence in its Lands' End rating.

transparency.note: The Commons' current Lands' End rating credits some public reporting but still flags disclosure gaps around suppliers, labor and impact targets.

durability.note: The brand emphasizes lasting quality and product care, but its sustainability evidence is stronger on durability claims than full supply-chain impact.

accessibility.note: Lands' End is a widely available mainstream retailer for family basics and school/work apparel.

products.name: PUMA
products.description: A globally recognizable athletic brand with unusually visible sustainability reporting for its size, but still a large new-product sportswear business.

environment.note: PUMA publishes annual sustainability reporting and targets, though its global sportswear footprint still depends heavily on high-volume new production.

labor.note: PUMA's human-rights page identifies supply-chain risk areas and says 2025 sourcing involved 141 independent suppliers in 27 countries.

transparency.note: PUMA discloses Tier 1 factories covering about 91% of apparel, footwear and accessories volume plus strategic Tier 2 factories.

durability.note: PUMA sells performance sportswear and footwear, but the cited sustainability materials emphasize reporting and supply chain more than repair or resale.

accessibility.note: PUMA is widely available globally through its own retail and mainstream sportswear channels.

products.name: New Balance
products.description: A mainstream athletic footwear and apparel brand with meaningful responsible-leadership disclosure, but not a repair-first or low-impact default.

environment.note: New Balance says it is working through RE100, the UN Fashion Industry Charter and ZDHC on environmental impacts across operations and supply chain.

labor.note: New Balance's supply-chain responsibility page sets human-rights targets around gender equality, fair compensation and forced labor.

transparency.note: The company publishes sustainability pages and a 2024 Sustainability and Impact Report, but disclosure depth is still below the most transparent apparel leaders.

durability.note: New Balance's strongest use-case is durable athletic footwear, but the public sustainability materials are not built around repair, resale or lifetime extension.

accessibility.note: New Balance is widely available through global retail and online channels, with a range from premium shoes to mainstream basics.

products.name: Under Armour
products.description: A familiar performance-apparel brand with some labor and sustainability structures, but a weaker transparency and circularity profile than stronger values-led picks.

environment.note: Under Armour publishes sustainability goals and reporting, but its public materials do not make it a low-impact or circular-apparel leader.

labor.note: Under Armour says it participates in the Fair Labor Association safeguard mechanism and has supplier-code and stakeholder-engagement processes.

transparency.note: Its 2023 sustainability materials identify supply-chain transparency as a material issue and reference supplier-list and human-rights commitments.

durability.note: Performance basics and athletic gear can be durable in use, but Under Armour is not presented as a repair, resale or long-life specialist.

accessibility.note: Under Armour is broadly available in mainstream sportswear retail and online channels, including frequent discounting.

products.name: Columbia Sportswear
products.description: A familiar outdoor brand with practical, durable gear strengths, but independent ratings flag limited current sustainability disclosure for its size.

environment.note: The Commons rates Columbia Insufficient, citing reliance on high-emissions materials and limited current sustainability efforts and disclosures.

labor.note: The Commons flags gaps in Columbia's code of conduct, living-wage language, grievance mechanisms and supply-chain auditing clarity.

transparency.note: Independent rating notes an overall lack of current sustainability efforts and disclosures for a brand of Columbia's size.

durability.note: The Commons notes Columbia offers repair services, warranties and a takeback program, supporting a stronger durability score than its disclosure score.

accessibility.note: Columbia is a widely available mainstream outdoor brand with broad online and retail availability.

products.name: Ralph Lauren
products.description: A premium mainstream brand with strong reporting infrastructure and an explicit timeless-design framing, but still a large commercial fashion company.

environment.note: Ralph Lauren's Timeless by Design strategy includes environment targets, reporting and policies, but it remains a large new-clothing business.

labor.note: Ralph Lauren publishes human-rights, foreign-migrant-worker, responsible-purchasing and supplier-engagement policies through its reports portal.

transparency.note: The company publishes a 2025 Global Citizenship & Sustainability Report plus GRI, SASB, TCFD and policy disclosures.

durability.note: Ralph Lauren frames its sustainability strategy around timeless products that can be worn, loved and passed on.

accessibility.note: Ralph Lauren is globally recognizable and widely available, but premium pricing lowers affordability compared with mainstream basics.
